flashcards.q: State the deterministic policy gradient theorem and explain what variance source it eliminates relative to the stochastic policy gradient theorem.
flashcards.a: grad_theta J = E_s[grad_a Q(s,a)|_{a=mu(s)} * grad_theta mu_theta(s)] -- pure chain rule, no expectation over sampled actions. It eliminates action-sampling variance entirely, since there's only one action (mu_theta(s)) per state, unlike the stochastic PG theorem's expectation over both states and actions.

flashcards.q: Why does a deterministic policy (DDPG/TD3) need externally added exploration noise?
flashcards.a: A deterministic policy outputs one exact action per state with no inherent randomness to explore with, unlike a stochastic policy that naturally explores by sampling -- exploration must be added externally (e.g. Gaussian noise on top of mu_theta(s) at data-collection time).

flashcards.q: Describe DDPG's core instability mechanism precisely.
flashcards.a: The actor's update direction is 'move toward whatever action the critic currently rates highest.' If the critic has any localized overestimation, the actor's gradient ascent walks straight into it and exploits it, and because the critic's own bootstrap target uses the actor's chosen next action, the overestimation can compound across updates rather than self-correct.

flashcards.q: Name TD3's three fixes and the specific failure mode each addresses.
flashcards.a: 1) Twin critics, take the min -- directly counters overestimation bias. 2) Delayed policy updates -- lets the critic stabilize before the actor exploits it. 3) Target policy smoothing -- removes sharp, exploitable Q-value peaks by regularizing the value surface.

flashcards.q: Why does TD3 use min-of-two-critics instead of Double DQN's selection/evaluation decoupling?
flashcards.a: Double DQN's fix relies on a discrete argmax operation to decouple between two networks. TD3's actor outputs a single continuous action directly -- there's no discrete argmax to decouple selection from, so taking the min of two independently-trained critics is used instead to directly dampen either critic's idiosyncratic overestimation.

flashcards.q: Write TD3's target policy smoothing formula and explain what specific problem it solves that twin critics do not.
flashcards.a: a~ = mu_target(s') + clip(noise, -c, c), noise ~ N(0, sigma^2). It fixes sharp, narrow, likely-spurious Q-value peaks a deterministic actor could converge onto and exploit -- a different, more local failure geometry than the twin critics' systemic overestimation fix.

flashcards.q: Write SAC's maximum entropy objective and explain why folding entropy into the value function is different from an entropy bonus added only to the policy loss.
flashcards.a: J(pi) = E[sum gamma^t (r_t + alpha*H[pi(.|s_t)])], with soft V(s) = E_a[Q(s,a) - alpha*log pi(a|s)]. Because entropy is inside the value function, it propagates through EVERY bootstrapped target, changing the actual fixed point -- unlike a bonus added only to the actor's loss, which never touches what the critic is trained to predict.

flashcards.q: Why doesn't SAC need target policy smoothing the way TD3 does?
flashcards.a: SAC's policy is inherently stochastic -- it samples from a genuinely spread-out distribution rather than committing to one point, so it structurally can't collapse onto and exploit a narrow, isolated Q-value peak the way a deterministic policy can.

flashcards.q: Derive SAC's automatic temperature tuning update and explain why log(alpha) is optimized rather than alpha directly.
flashcards.a: J(alpha) = E[-alpha*(log pi(a|s) + H_bar)], target entropy H_bar commonly set to -|A|. This pushes alpha up when policy entropy is below target, down when above. log(alpha) is optimized instead of alpha to guarantee alpha > 0 automatically via exp(), without a separate positivity constraint.

flashcards.q: Do TD3 or SAC address the sim-to-real transfer gap or hard safety constraints natively?
flashcards.a: No -- neither addresses simulator-vs-reality dynamics mismatch (needs domain randomization) or hard safety constraints (needs a constrained MDP/Lagrangian formulation or a shielding mechanism at execution time). Both optimize an unconstrained expected-return-style objective for whatever dynamics they're trained against.

flashcards.q: State the real production hyperparameter defaults: TD3 delayed update ratio, smoothing noise/clip, Polyak tau, SAC target entropy.
flashcards.a: TD3 policy_delay d=2. Smoothing noise sigma~0.2, clip~0.5. Polyak averaging tau~0.005. SAC target entropy heuristic H_bar ~ -|A| (negative action dimensionality).
